problem: Collecting more repetitive demonstrations may not improve single-task generalization to genuinely new objects and environments.
contribution: A controlled real-world scaling study separates environment diversity, object diversity and repetitions, then proposes a task-dependent data-collection strategy.
algorithm: TrainDiffusionPolicy on datasets parameterized by environmentcountM, objectcountN and repetitionsK. Evaluate on unseen environments/objects, fit empirical scaling relationships and test a collectionstrategy; this is an empirical scaling result, not a guarantee for arbitrary tasks.
observations: UMI-collected visual demonstrations with pose/trajectory reconstruction; trained visuomotor observations depend on thechosen policy/cameras.
actions: UMI gripper trajectories mapped into robot motion through thepolicyinterface;SLAMvalidity and temporalalignment are prerequisites.
embodiment_and_data: RealPourWater andMouseArrangement scaling tasks, with additionalFoldTowels andUnplugCharger verification. Demonstrations span many real scenes and object instances; about90%collectedUMIdemonstrations were valid according to thepaper.
experiments: VaryM,N,K, compare novel-object/novel-environment generalization, randomized policyrollout order with matched initialconditions, and visualencoder/actionhead scaling andfine-tuning choices.
baselines: Dataset-size/diversity conditions and architecture/fine-tuning alternatives; repetitions and diversity are separated rather than simply comparing total framecounts.

quantitative_result.finding: For the studiedM16,N64 setting, performance plateaus near800trainingdemonstrations; for8/16/32environment-objectpairs, saturation is reported near400/800/1600demonstrations.
quantitative_result.unverified_prediction: Page8predicts1191pairs for0.99normalizedMouseArrangement score and explicitly leaves verification to futurework.

limitations: Single-taskILscaling does not establish language/task-level generalization or cross-embodiment transfer. Powerlaw extrapolations beyond observeddata are predictions. UMI failures in texture-poor scenes and incomplete valid demonstrations affect usabledata.
hardware_adaptation: Use diversity-aware teachingguidance and session/object provenance. A smallNX baseline can test saturation locally without reproducing a largeencoder; never promise broadgeneralization from a few repeatedepisodes.
algorithm_detail: The study independently varies diverse environment/object coverage and within-condition demonstrations, so a powerlaw with diversity is not evidence of a powerlaw with framecount. Matchedinitialconditions and randomized policyselection reduce evaluatorbias; normalizedscore is distinct from binarysuccess.
integration_contract: Dataset manifests need environment, objectinstance, session, repetition andvalidity fields. Protocols must define unseenobjects/scenes before collection and keep policyselection away from finaltest conditions.
license_evidence: PrimaryICLR2025/arXivfulltext inspected; no officialcode or data/modellicense audit completed. Published collectionideas may inform protocol design, but no code reuse rights are inferred.
required_experiments: Smallpilot measuring repeatversusdiversity effects under equalvalid-episode budgets; separate heldoutobject/scene splits; report invalidcapture rate andactual independentattempt counts; keep extrapolated trends labeledpredictions.
difference_from_explorer: Diversity-aware collection and scaling are already studied. Explorer's H1must disentangle sourcecompatibility from simply adding more scenes, objects orcompute.
